function: Multi-agent A3C selects beam-hopping patterns (cells illuminated) across LEO satellites for load balancing; MADDPG allocates power per beam; LSTM predicts cell traffic (p. 1, 6-9).
system: Ka-band (20 GHz) forward link of 12 LEO satellites at 780 km, 4 beams each, 19 cells per satellite, 100 MHz, full frequency reuse (p. 4, 10).
method: Two-tier multi-agent DRL: A3C with actor-critic per satellite and cloud global critic for beam hopping; MADDPG for per-beam power; LSTM trained on historical demand for prediction (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space path loss with beam antenna gain, clear sky; parameters from Table II citing [45]; no dataset or measurements stated (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Trained 6000 episodes per Table II; the trained model with alpha=beta=0.5 is compared with baselines versus total traffic demand; no unseen-scenario test (p. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: greedy, random, periodic, queue-length beam hopping; RBH-FP and RBH-DP (random hopping, fixed or demand-based power); learned: FPA (BH only), DPA (discretized joint RL) (p. 10-11).
metrics: Throughput, load balance (satellite load gap), average queueing delay, delay fairness; training reward and loss (p. 10-12).
complexity: Big-O complexity of the LSTM, A3C and MADDPG parts and of the whole algorithm (p. 9); no measured runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "clear sky conditions prevail, neglecting rain attenuation" - own free-space channel with antenna gains [39]; no 3GPP TR 38.811 model, no measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "To strike a balance between load and delay fairness, we use the trained model with" - evaluation of the trained model in the same simulated setup; no unseen constellation, band or traffic pattern is stated (demand sweeps in Figs. 8 and 10 are not described as unseen).
q3_support: p. 10: "In DPA, each satellite acts as an agent, completing BH and PA (discretized processing)" - the only learned comparators are FPA (the proposed beam hopping with fixed power, an ablation) and DPA (the authors' own joint discretized variant, no named standard algorithm or earlier paper); all other baselines are non-learned.

q5_support: p. 9: "In this paper, we simulate a Ka-band forward BH and PA system" - self-built simulation; no code or data link, no public dataset or measurements are stated.
notes: Area 6: LEO beam hopping and power allocation learned by DRL; in satellite links learned control of beams and power is physical layer, and the LSTM traffic prediction only supports beam hopping. q3 is borderline: DPA is an RL-based joint scheme with discretized power defined by the authors (algorithm unnamed, no earlier citation) and FPA is the proposed method without its power module; both treated as variants, so no learned baseline counts; reviewer to confirm. q2: the traffic-demand sweeps are not stated as unseen conditions.
